lore_anchors.definition: A high-tier artifact refined from a cultivator’s life essence, possessing power far exceeding common magic tools. It is often bound to the user’s soul and can only be properly wielded by cultivators of a certain rank.
A natal magic tool used by Han Li to control and command soulless bodies, such as the zombie Qu Hun. Its power can be resisted by strong spiritual defenses.
A powerful, concentrated offensive technique that fires a drill-like projectile of pure energy. It is a high-cost, high-damage attack resource in Han Li’s arsenal.

The crystallized essence of a Core Formation cultivator’s power and lifespan. It is the literal core of their being, and its destruction is both a fatal blow and a potential source of powerful fragmented remains.
A genuine Magical Treasure, likely the former weapon of a Core Formation cultivator. It is Han Li’s first treasure of this tier, but he lacks the cultivation base to activate it.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why couldn't Han Li just kill Qu Hun directly?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He was unsure if Qu Hun's zombie body had vital points like a normal person, so he chose to attack the seemingly invulnerable green orb, which turned out to be the target's true weak point.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why can't Han Li use the Green煌 Sword right away?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In the cultivation world, Magical Treasures are soul-bound to high-level users. Without a Core Formation cultivation base, a Foundation Establishment cultivator lacks the power to break that seal or fuel the treasure's immense energy demands.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What are the fragments Han Li picks up at the end?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They are the remains of the green orb, which Han Li suspects are pieces of the original cultivator's Golden Core. They may hold residual power or secrets, making them a dangerous but potentially valuable asset.
